fivem-restore.name: Restore default services and registry
fivem-restore.desc: Puts everything back to Windows defaults to pass the PC check. Recommended for FiveM.
fivem-restore.help: Many optimizers turn off services that FiveM servers inspect during the PC check, and that can look like you are hiding something. This: (1) undoes the SmoothTwk tweaks that turned those services off, if you applied them; (2) sets PcaSvc, DPS, DiagTrack, SysMain, EventLog, BFE, CDPSvc, DusmSvc to automatic and Appinfo, SSDPSRV, UmRdpService to manual, which is how they ship in Windows, and starts them; (3) sets BAM, Prefetch and the Program Compatibility Assistant to their default values. Some changes finish applying after a restart. It is the same as the "Activar servicios" (Enable services) option in the Servicios.rar file, without RemoteRegistry.

fivem-cache.name: Clear FiveM cache
fivem-cache.desc: Only if you get slow loading, broken textures or join errors. It won't raise FPS.
fivem-cache.warn: Close FiveM first. The next time you join a server, FiveM downloads its files again.
fivem-cache.help: FiveM stores each server's files in its cache folder. Over time it grows a lot and can cause slow loading, missing textures or errors when joining. This deletes the cache, server-cache and server-cache-priv folders inside FiveM.app\data. It does not delete your settings, your keybinds or your account. FiveM recreates them on its own.

restore-point.name: Create restore point
restore-point.desc: The safest option: saves a copy of the system so you can roll back if something breaks.
restore-point.help: Saves a "snapshot" of your Windows configuration: registry, drivers, installed programs and system files. If something stops working after a tweak, you can go back to how it was from Start > "Create a restore point" > System Restore, or from Maintenance > Classic panels > Windows Restore. Your documents, photos and games are not touched. It's the first thing worth doing before optimizing. If System Protection was off on C:, SmoothTwk turns it on (it uses a bit of disk space). Windows normally allows one point every 24 hours; SmoothTwk lifts that limit only while it creates the point and then puts it back as it was.

fix-wu.name: Reset Windows Update
fix-wu.desc: Stops the services, clears the download cache and starts them again.
fix-wu.help: If Windows Update gets stuck or throws errors, this stops its services, renames the update download folder and starts them again. Windows downloads whatever it needs again. Restart your PC afterwards.

fix-net.name: Reset network
fix-net.desc: Resets Winsock and TCP/IP and flushes the DNS cache. Requires a restart.
fix-net.help: If the internet works badly or won't connect, this resets Windows' network configuration (Winsock and TCP/IP) and clears the DNS cache. Your saved Wi-Fi networks are not deleted. Restart your PC afterwards.

fix-ntp.name: Sync time with pool.ntp.org
fix-ntp.desc: Syncs your clock with more accurate public time servers.
fix-ntp.help: Switches the Windows time server (time.windows.com) to pool.ntp.org, which is usually more accurate, and syncs the clock now.

fix-winget.name: Repair WinGet
fix-winget.desc: Reinstalls the package manager used by the Apps section.
fix-winget.help: WinGet is the installer used by the Apps section. If it fails, this reinstalls it by downloading it from Microsoft.

fix-sfc.name: System file scan
fix-sfc.desc: DISM and SFC repair damaged files. Takes 10 to 30 minutes.
fix-sfc.help: Checks Windows files and repairs any that are damaged. First DISM repairs the Windows image (it downloads files from Windows Update), then SFC checks the system. Takes 10 to 30 minutes; don't turn off the PC while it runs.

fix-trim.name: Optimize SSD (TRIM)
fix-trim.desc: Sends TRIM to the system drive. Safe and fast.
fix-trim.help: TRIM tells the SSD which space is now free so it stays fast. Windows does this on its own once a week; this does it now. It's safe and takes seconds.

wu-default.name: Default updates
wu-default.desc: Removes update policies and leaves Windows as it ships.
wu-default.help: Removes any Windows Update policy set by SmoothTwk or other programs, and leaves updates as they come out of the box.

wu-security.name: Security only
wu-security.desc: Security patches after 4 days, new versions a year later, and no drivers.
wu-security.help: Windows installs security patches 4 days after they come out, delays big versions (like 24H2 or 25H2) by one year and doesn't update drivers on its own. It's a middle ground between stability and security.

wpffeaturesdotnet.help: Enables .NET Framework 3.5 (includes 2.0 and 3.0) and 4.x. Some older programs and games won't open without it.

fivem.tagline: PC check and performance · GTA V Legacy on DirectX 11

guide.name: Screen Type
guide.why: True fullscreen reaches your monitor faster than windowed mode.

guide.name: VSync
guide.why: VSync waits for the display before showing each frame, and that adds delay.

guide.name: DirectX Version
guide.why: It's the version GTA V Legacy runs best on inside FiveM.

guide.name: MSAA and Reflection MSAA
guide.why: MSAA anti-aliasing is among the heaviest settings in the game.

guide.name: Grass Quality
guide.why: High grass quality is one of the biggest FPS drains.

guide.name: Extended Distance Scaling
guide.why: Draws less distant detail: raises FPS in the city.

guide.name: Population Density / Variety
guide.why: Fewer people and cars spawned by the game, if the server allows it.

guide.name: Ambient Occlusion
guide.why: Expensive contact shadows with little value for gameplay.

guide.name: High Detail Streaming While Flying
guide.why: Prevents stutters when flying or going very fast.

guide.name: Texture Quality
guide.why: Textures cost almost no FPS if your card has enough memory.

guide.name: Motion Blur Strength
guide.why: No blur when moving: you see other players better.

guide.name: Anisotropic Filtering
guide.why: Sharp ground at a distance for very little cost.

guide.name: F8 console: cl_drawperf true
guide.why: Shows FPS, ping and packet loss while you play. Keep in mind many servers cap FPS with their scripts.

cautions: Legend Division requires Secure Boot and TPM. Since October 2026 that playlist requires Secure Boot and TPM enabled; regular Ranked and Casual don't yet. Don't turn them off in the BIOS.
Don't use macros. Ubisoft has detected macros and input manipulation since Year 11: SmoothTwk includes nothing of the sort.
Process priority: leave it as is. BattlEye protects the process and there's no guarantee about changing it.

guide.name: Display Mode
guide.why: The most direct path to your screen.

guide.name: V-Sync
guide.why: Syncing to the monitor adds delay.

guide.name: NVIDIA Reflex Low Latency
guide.why: Shortens the GPU frame queue. It's not confirmed to exist in Siege X: only enable it if you see it in the menu.

guide.name: Frame Rate Limit
guide.value: Unlimited (or 3 below your Hz with G-Sync)
guide.why: Keeps the GPU queue short; with G-Sync/FreeSync it keeps you inside the range.

guide.name: Render Scaling
guide.why: Stable, sharp image.

guide.name: Adaptive Render Scaling
guide.why: Stops the resolution from changing on its own mid-fight.

guide.name: Shading Quality
guide.why: Big FPS gain with little visual change.

guide.name: Shadow Quality
guide.why: Some pros use Medium because shadows give away opponents.

guide.name: Reflection Quality / Ambient Occlusion
guide.why: Expensive and no competitive value.

guide.name: Texture Quality
guide.why: Depends on your card's memory.

guide.name: LOD Quality
guide.why: Distant objects look the same as up close.

guide.name: Lens Effects / Zoom-In Depth of Field
guide.why: Less glare and blur when aiming.

guide.name: Anti-Aliasing
guide.why: Clean edges without losing detail; DLAA or FSR Native if available.

cautions: Vanguard requires TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot. Without them you get the VAN 9001 or VAN 9003 errors. Don't turn off virtualization-based security. The "Turn off VBS and memory integrity" tweak in Advanced security can lock you out of this game or out of its tournaments.
Vanguard may require memory integrity (HVCI) and IOMMU. If you see VAN:RESTRICTION, turn back on whatever it asks for.
Process priority: leave it as is. There's no confirmation that changing it is safe with Vanguard.

guide.name: Display Mode
guide.why: The lowest latency in a DirectX 11 game.

guide.name: NVIDIA Reflex Low Latency
guide.why: Shortens the GPU frame queue. Use On if your minimum FPS drops.

guide.name: VSync
guide.why: Syncing to the monitor adds delay.

guide.name: Limit FPS Always
guide.why: Lets the game run as fast as it can; set it a bit above your Hz if your CPU can't keep up.

guide.name: Raw Input Buffer
guide.why: In General > Mouse: less mouse delay, especially at 1000 Hz or more.

guide.name: Multithreaded Rendering
guide.why: Uses multiple cores; try it if you have 4 or more.

guide.name: Material / Texture / Detail / UI Quality
guide.why: More FPS with very little change for competitive play.

guide.name: Vignette / Cast Shadows
guide.why: Effects that cost FPS and don't help you see.

guide.name: Anti-Aliasing
guide.why: Clean edges at low cost.

guide.name: Anisotropic Filtering
guide.why: Sharp floors and walls at an angle.

guide.name: Improve Clarity
guide.value: Off (On if you have FPS to spare)
guide.why: Helps visibility, but costs FPS.

guide.name: Bloom / Distortion
guide.why: Less visual noise in fights.

guide.name: Network Buffering
guide.why: What happens in the match reaches you sooner.

guide.name: Client FPS / Network RTT (Stats)
guide.why: To keep an eye on FPS and ping while you play.

cautions: Tournaments require TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot. For tournaments at level 350 or higher since 2025, and reportedly for all tournaments (plus IOMMU) since February 2026. Regular matches don't. Don't turn off virtualization-based security. The "Turn off VBS and memory integrity" tweak in Advanced security can lock you out of this game or out of its tournaments.
Don't set GameUserSettings.ini to read-only. Epic warns that graphics and Performance Mode changes won't be saved that way.

guide.name: Window Mode
guide.why: True fullscreen responds faster.

guide.name: NVIDIA Reflex Low Latency
guide.why: Shortens the GPU frame queue.

guide.name: V-Sync
guide.why: Syncing to the monitor adds delay.

guide.name: Frame Rate Limit
guide.why: Epic recommends matching your Hz only if you see screen tearing.

guide.name: Rendering Mode
guide.why: Epic's competitive mode: turns off almost all effects.

guide.name: Shadows
guide.why: Shadows are among the most expensive settings.

guide.name: Effects / Post Processing
guide.why: Fewer effects on top of the action.

guide.name: Textures / Meshes
guide.why: Depends on your card's memory.

guide.name: Pre-download Streamed Assets
guide.why: Downloads textures before the match: fewer stutters.

guide.name: 3D Resolution
guide.why: Sharp image at your real resolution.

guide.name: View Distance
guide.why: You see buildings and players at a distance.

guide.name: Motion Blur
guide.why: No blur when turning.

guide.name: Anti-Aliasing & Super Resolution
guide.why: Only use TSR or DLSS if your GPU can't reach the FPS you want.

warzone.tagline: Inside Call of Duty HQ · DirectX 12 · Ricochet
cautions: TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot are mandatory. Warzone has required them since December 2025, with UEFI BIOS and a GPT disk; Intel PTT or AMD fTPM work. Don't turn off virtualization-based security. The "Turn off VBS and memory integrity" tweak in Advanced security can lock you out of this game or out of its tournaments.
There's an extra device verification. Since June 2026, if you fail the verification you're limited to casual modes.
Process priority: leave it as is. Ricochet runs at kernel level and there's no confirmation about that change.

guide.name: Display Mode
guide.why: Exclusive fullscreen is the fastest.

guide.name: NVIDIA Reflex Low Latency
guide.why: Or AMD Anti-Lag 2 if available. Shortens the GPU queue.

guide.name: V-Sync (Gameplay and Menus)
guide.why: Syncing to the monitor adds delay.

guide.name: Custom Frame Rate Limit
guide.why: Steady pacing without leaving the G-Sync/FreeSync range.

guide.name: Frame Generation
guide.why: Makes up in-between frames and adds delay.

guide.name: Render Resolution / Dynamic Resolution
guide.why: Fixed, sharp resolution.

guide.name: Upscaling / Sharpening
guide.value: FidelityFX CAS (DLSS/FSR Quality if GPU falls short)
guide.why: Nearly free sharpness; upscaling only if you need more FPS.

guide.name: VRAM Scale Target
guide.why: Prevents stutters from running out of video memory.

guide.name: Shader / Shadow Quality
guide.why: The heaviest settings in the game.

guide.name: Screen-Space Shadows / Ambient Occlusion / Reflections
guide.why: Expensive effects with no competitive value.

guide.name: On-Demand Texture Streaming
guide.why: Fewer stutters from disk and network.

guide.name: Depth of Field / Motion Blur
guide.why: No blur when aiming or turning.

guide.name: Film Grain
guide.why: Removes the grain that muddies the image.

guide.name: First-Person Camera Movement
guide.why: The camera moves less when running.

cautions: Minecraft has no anti-cheat on your PC. Each server has its own rules: check whether it allows mods like Sodium before using them.
Dedicated GPU applies to the launcher's Java. It's the classic fix when Minecraft runs on the integrated graphics on laptops.

guide.name: Fullscreen
guide.why: Fullscreen responds faster.

guide.name: VSync
guide.why: Syncing to the monitor adds delay.

guide.name: Max Framerate
guide.why: Lets the game run as fast as it can.

guide.name: Raw Input
guide.why: In Mouse Settings: the mouse responds without the Windows filter.

guide.name: Graphics
guide.why: Fast mode removes expensive effects.

guide.name: Render Distance
guide.why: It's what affects FPS the most.

guide.name: Simulation Distance
guide.why: Fewer active chunks: less CPU load.

guide.name: Clouds / Particles / Entity Shadows
guide.why: Effects that cost FPS and don't help you play.

guide.name: Biome Blend
guide.why: Saves CPU when loading terrain.

guide.name: Launcher RAM (-Xmx)
guide.why: In the profile > JVM arguments. Never more than half your RAM: too much causes pauses.

guide.name: Performance mods (Fabric)
guide.why: They replace the rendering engine and game logic with faster versions. Get them from Modrinth for your exact version.

guide.name: FOV
guide.why: More peripheral vision without too much distortion.

guide.name: Mipmap Levels
guide.why: Sharper distant blocks.

guide.name: Bedrock: Vibrant Visuals / Fancy Graphics
guide.why: On the Bedrock edition: more FPS with a shorter render distance.
